items.finding: The source states that OH bands in NIR and MIR are temperature-sensitive when measuring aqueous solutions, so tempered sample holders are necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For the MIR ATR option, this supports measuring or controlling stream temperature at the probe and testing temperature variation during the comparison.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review of biopharmaceutical downstream processing and refers to aqueous solutions, not a petroleum stream; it does not establish an in-line temperature-sensor design.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: In the cited study, temperature was varied together with concentration and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This supports treating temperature as a calibration variable and checking it at the measurement point when assessing the MIR ATR option.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not petroleum; it is model-development evidence rather than proof of an in-line temperature sensor.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as combining inputs by placing variables from different sources one after the other in a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: For the extended MIR ATR option, this is a basis for testing whether synchronised MIR-ATR and NIR variables can be concatenated and whether the fused model beats the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general review of data fusion in process analytical technology, not a petroleum study, and the quoted paragraph does not address block scaling or probe synchronisation.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E03 ¶31

items.finding: The source says that before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This supports a first comparison that checks whether NIR adds useful information to MIR ATR before keeping the extra method in the fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general review, not a petroleum-stream experiment; it does not show that fusion will improve performance for this application.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82
